content.title: About
content.content: Creamy peanut butter is a smooth paste made from roasted peanuts, usually without added nut pieces. It has a velvety texture and a mild nutty flavor, suitable for spreading, cooking, and baking.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Peanut butter originated in the United States in the early 1900s and quickly became a popular quick‑snack food.
The creamy (smooth) version differs from chunky by adding vegetable oils to eliminate peanut fragments.
Peanuts are legumes, not true nuts, although they are treated as nuts in culinary contexts.
In the U.S. more than 5 million tonnes of peanut butter are consumed each year.
Peanut butter is a staple in sports nutrition because of its high protein and fast‑acting carbohydrate content.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: One tablespoon of creamy peanut butter provides about 4 g of protein, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Source of healthy fats
items.content: Most of the fat is monounsaturated and polyunsaturated, which are heart‑friendly.

items.title: Contains vitamin E
items.content: Vitamin E acts as an antioxidant, protecting cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Provides magnesium
items.content: Magnesium supports muscle and nerve function and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Sustains energy
items.content: The blend of fats, protein, and a small amount of carbs offers lasting satiety and steady energy.

items.title: Peanut allergy
items.content: Peanut butter can trigger severe allergic reactions, including anaphylaxis.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: One tablespoon contains roughly 90 kcal, so portion control is important.

items.title: Added salt and sugar
items.content: Some varieties contain extra salt or sugar, which may be undesirable for hypertension or diabetes.

items.title: Aflatoxins
items.content: Poor‑quality peanuts can be contaminated with aflatoxins, toxic mycotoxins, so choose reputable brands.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Spread peanut butter on toast, use it in sauces, smoothies, baked goods, or stir it into oatmeal and yogurt. For a thicker consistency, gently warm it.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in a tightly sealed jar in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, refrigerate to slow fat oxidation. Discard if it develops a rancid smell.
